proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the absence of ontological orientation'?

entities.label: AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation
entities.rationale: The phrase 'absence of ontological orientation' most plausibly denotes a theoretical/informational content — a characterization of a system or entity as lacking a property of directedness toward an ontological ground. As a propositional or theoretical content (a pattern that can be multiply instantiated and copied), it fits best as a Generically Dependent Continuant. It is not a process (it does not unfold), not a quality or disposition (it is not directly borne by a single individual as an SDC without further analysis), and not a material entity. However, see open_questions: there are genuine alternatives depending on intended use.

open_questions: Is 'absence of ontological orientation' intended as a theoretical concept/content (a claim or characterization in a legal or philosophical theory), in which case BFO_0000031 (GDC) is most apt?

Or is it intended as a quality of a specific legal institution or system — i.e., a property that inheres in a particular bearer? In that case it would be typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) or Disposition (BFO_0000016), specifically a privative quality (lack of a disposition).

BFO 2020 does not natively model absences or privations as positive entities; should we model this as a negation/complement of an existing class such as working:OntologicalPrimacyClaim or a missing working:OntologicalOrientation disposition, rather than as a positive class?

Should 'ontological orientation' itself be minted first as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — a capacity of a legal system to be directed toward a normative or ontological ground — so that its absence is a privation of that disposition inhering in a bearer?
Is this concept intended to be an individual (e.g., a named thesis or principle in a specific theory) or a class (a kind that can have multiple instances)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'absence of ontological orientation' is philosophically complex and ontologically ambiguous. In BFO 2020, there is no native category for absences or privations; BFO models what positively exists. The most defensible positive classification depends on intended use: (1) If this denotes a theoretical content — a claim that some system lacks ontological grounding — it is a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031), parallel to other theoretical items in the working ontology such as NaturalLawExplanatoryGap or OntologicalValidityThesis. (2) If it denotes a property that inheres in a specific legal institution (a measurable lack of directedness), it is better modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) — a privative quality — borne by that institution. (3) If it denotes a missing capacity, one should first mint 'OntologicalOrientation' as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) and then represent the absence relationally or via negation in OWL (i.e., a legal institution that does NOT bear an instance of OntologicalOrientation). Given conservatism (Rule 7) and the theoretical context of the working ontology, the proposal mints AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation as a GDC class, but flags all alternatives in open_questions before any commitment is made.
